basic_identification.full_title: Door Handles for Mortice Locks — Specification (Second Revision)

scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for materials, dimensions, manufacture, workmanship, finish, and performance-testing for door handles (lever door handles and door knobs) used with mortice locks.

revision_history.edition: Second Revision (overhauls testing guidelines, updates material chemistry, and introduces the 6-digit classification coding system)

amendment_slips.description: Modifies marking and labeling clauses: substitutes Clause 8.1 (a) to require the 'Manufacturer’s name or brand name or trade mark' instead of the previous text; substitutes Clause 9.1 (a) to require 'Manufacturer’s name or brand name or trade name'; and deletes Clause 9.1 (b) completely.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Door Fittings (Quality Control) Order', all door handles for mortice locks must conform to IS 4992:2024 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, or sold in India.

requirements.detail: Every certified door handle/knob and its packaging box must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the CM/L licence number.
Under Amendment No. 1 (May 2026), Clause 8.1 (a) is modified to require that each individual door handle be clearly and indelibly marked with the 'Manufacturer's name or brand name or trade mark'.

Under Amendment No. 1 (May 2026), Clause 9.1 (a) is modified to require that each packaging carton be marked with the 'Manufacturer's name or brand name or trade name', while the previous packaging marking requirement under Clause 9.1 (b) is completely deleted.
Covers two main types: a) Lever door handles; b) Door knobs.
Handles must withstand high pulling forces (tested using axial strength apparatus with tension loads up to 1000 N) without stripping threads, breaking, or pulling loose from the spindle.

The spring return mechanism must withstand high durability cyclic testing (up to 200,000 operations depending on durability grade) with zero structural failures, loss of return angle, or spring slippage.
Handles must withstand neutral salt spray testing (up to 240 hours depending on grade) to ensure corrosion resistance on finishes (plated, painted, or anodised layers).

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 4992 : 2024 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing door handles and knobs used with mortice locks. Formulated under India's statutory Door Fittings Quality Control Order (QCO), all such handles must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to verify mechanical safety, fire-resistance, and long-term durability. This edition, incorporating Amendment No. 1 (May 2026), refines marking rules to standardise the labeling of manufacturer and brand names on both the handles and their retail packaging cartons. It establishes a 6-digit classification code rating handles on category of use, durability cycling (up to 200,000 cycles), fire safety, and salt spray corrosion resistance, verifying that they can sustain severe axial pull forces (up to 1000 N) without failing.
